# Börsen trotsar oron – Analyschefen: ”Kommer krävas mer”

**Feed**: borslunch  
**Published**: 2026-09-16  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

Börslunch (EFN) talks to Mikael Sarve, strategist and head of analysis at SB1. Although he usually leans pessimistic, he is cautiously optimistic this time. He expects the market to level off after a strong year and sees no strong macro trigger for a real sell-off, but he is wary of the usual September–October weakness, inflation near 4%, rising real rates and very loose US fiscal policy. For now he would rather hold US investment-grade credit yielding over 6% and add equities around the end of October. The episode also includes an interview with Aker BP's CFO on production growth from 2027 and physical oil prices above the futures price, plus a brief positive note on medtech after comments from Thermo Fisher.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 ENGCON-B — Engcon | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Danske Bank issued a buy recommendation, calling Engcon well positioned for a recovery; the stock rose 6%.

#### Reasoning

This is a cited analyst view from Danske Bank, not the hosts' or the guest's own opinion. The case is a cyclical recovery for Engcon's markets, in line with the episode's view that cyclical sectors are turning up, especially in Sweden. The recommendation was reported only in the news segment, so conviction is moderate.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the cyclical recovery stalls
- if rising real rates hit construction and machinery demand
- if Danske Bank downgrades

> *"Engcon upp 6 % på en köprekommendation från Danske Bank, som säger att bolaget är välpositionerat för en återhämtning."*

---

### 🟠 AKRBP — Aker BP | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 40%

The CFO expects production to rise >35% from 2027 and gas output to double; physical oil sells well above futures prices; the company is open to M&A.

#### Reasoning

The positive view comes from company management (the CFO), not from the hosts or an independent analyst. The case rests on Yggdrasil and Fenris starting production in summer 2027, a realised oil price of up to ~$150/bbl during the Middle East disruption, and possible value-creating M&A. The stock is already up 50%+ YTD and nobody in the studio gave an explicit recommendation.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Yggdrasil/Fenris start-up is delayed
- if the Middle East situation eases and physical oil premiums collapse
- if an acquisition destroys value

> *"Då vill produktionen öka med över 35 % de nästa par åren."*
